title: Microscope Slides in Motion — source and archive registry supplement 06

records.institution: Museo Nacional de Ciencias Naturales, CSIC
records.collection: Legado Cajal — microscopic preparations and documentary collections
records.type: scientist archive + histological slide collection + digital catalogue
records.date_scope: late nineteenth–twentieth century; deposited at MNCN in 2023
records.holdings: The Cajal Legacy contains more than 28,000 scientific and personal objects, including thousands of histological preparations, scientific drawings, manuscripts, photographs, books, furniture, and instruments. Individual slide records in CSIC Simurg preserve physical description, method, condition, handwritten or printed labels, multiple historical inventory numbers, original cabinet/tray location, present archival call number, and current custody information.
records.research_use: An unusually explicit case of object re-addressing. A single preparation can retain its original laboratory address (for example preparation cabinet and tray), later museum/institute inventory numbers, a current Legado Cajal reference, and a modern archival call number. The collection also preserves commercial teaching slides used alongside Cajal-school preparations.
records.access: The legacy is available for research; MNCN's current collection page links to the Legado Cajal catalogue in CSIC Simurg and provides a dedicated research contact.

records.institution: Museo per la Storia dell'Università, University of Pavia
records.collection: Camillo Golgi preparations, manuscripts, drawings, instruments, and archive
records.holdings: The Golgi Room preserves microscopic preparations, handwritten documents, drawings, instruments, and Golgi's malaria microscope slides. The museum history records the bequest of Golgi's heirlooms together with a large archive and notes that the museum itself preserves documentary material spanning the fifteenth to twentieth centuries.
records.research_use: Direct slide↔manuscript↔drawing↔instrument route for reconstructing histological practice and the later museum framing of a scientist's working legacy. It is a controlled comparator to Cajal because original preparations and documentary material survive within the same university museum system.
records.access: Museum and archival research by arrangement through the University of Pavia museum system.

records.institution: University of Florence — Museo Anatomico Fiorentino
records.collection: Filippo Pacini histological and microscopic preparations
records.type: historical slide collection + labelled research preparations
records.holdings: The museum preserves a carefully catalogued histological collection made by Filippo Pacini. Many slides carry dates, preparation substances, annotations, reflections, and doubts. The cholera preparations are especially well documented: labels refer directly to Pacini's published 1854 case descriptions, and at least one records that the preparation was remounted in new glass seven years after it was first made.
records.research_use: Exceptional object-level evidence for treating slide labels as compact laboratory records and publication cross-references. The remounting note also makes material repair/reformatting visible inside the historical object rather than only in modern conservation files.
records.access: Museum research through the University of Florence Department of Experimental and Clinical Medicine.

records.holdings: The BNCF Pacini fonds consists of 23 units preserving Filippo Pacini's papers. It was acquired for the National Library in 1885. The Library identifies Aurelio Bianchi's 1889 Relazione e catalogo dei manoscritti di Filippo Pacini as the historical access instrument.
records.research_use: Documentary companion to the surviving University of Florence preparations. The historical manuscript catalogue creates a tractable route for connecting Pacini's labelled slides, methods, research notes, publication claims, correspondence, and the posthumous dispersal of his scientific legacy between institutions.
records.access: Manuscript and rare-book consultation through BNCF; the historical catalogue is identified by the library as the principal access instrument.

records.collection: Anatomy Department historical records: preparations, microscopes, manufacture catalogues, and practical microscopy
records.type: institutional archive + preparation inventory + microscope records
records.holdings: The Anatomy Department document list preserves a preparation quantity ledger for 1878–1882 (no. 118), a microscope and instrument index for 1879–1881 (no. 119), a catalogue of manufactured histology and embryology items for 1880–1883 (no. 120), practical microscopy miscellanea for 1882–1884 (no. 121), microscope records for 1873–1884 and 1883 (nos. 122–123), a histology course diary for 1882–1884 (no. 110), and a later instrument survey book for 1887 (no. 127).
records.research_use: One of the strongest surviving institutional paper trails for nineteenth-century slide production and use outside Europe. It can connect preparation quantities, manufacture, instruments, practical teaching, and course administration within one anatomy department before the 1895 Japanese commercial slide advertisement already identified in the bibliography.
records.access: Historical holdings are described by the University of Tokyo Medical Library; consultation follows library special-collection procedures.

records.collection: Pieter Harting microscopy collection and nineteenth-century teaching heritage
records.date_scope: principally nineteenth century with later collection development
records.holdings: The museum identifies Pieter Harting as the professor who expanded and mapped the university's unique microscopy collection and as a pioneer of practical microscopy teaching around 1845. The present microscopy collection includes hundreds of microscopes and associated objects, while museum interpretation also identifies surviving Harting preparations within the historical collections.
records.research_use: A direct route into the material infrastructure of early university microscopy teaching: instruments, preparations, collection mapping, and pedagogy can be studied together without reducing the case to instrument history alone.
records.access: Collection research through Universiteitsmuseum Utrecht; substantial collection histories are published online.

records.institution: University of Antwerp heritage network / Meise Botanic Garden / Ghent Museum for the History of Sciences
records.collection: Henri Van Heurck scientific estate and diatom/microscopy collections
records.type: distributed scientific estate + diatom collection + microscopy heritage
records.date_scope: second half of nineteenth century; estate reallocated during twentieth–twenty-first centuries
records.holdings: Van Heurck assembled a major botanical library, herbarium, diatom collection, scientific equipment, and an internationally exceptional microscope collection. Antwerp's heritage history records purchase of his estate by the city in 1910 and its later dispersal: books to the Hendrik Conscience Heritage Library, botanical material to Meise Botanic Garden, and scientific instruments including microscopes to Ghent. Meise confirms that its herbarium includes microscopic preparations and important nineteenth-century collections including Van Heurck, and preserves his major diatom holdings.
records.research_use: A large-scale institutional re-addressing case. Instead of one slide being renumbered inside a cabinet, a scientist's integrated working collection was progressively divided by material/disciplinary category across institutions. It offers a direct comparator for the later disassembly of hybrid object-text collections.
records.access: Research routes depend on component: Antwerp heritage documentation, Meise botanical/diatom collections, Hendrik Conscience library holdings, and Ghent scientific instruments.

records.collection: Edward Heron-Allen foraminifera slide collection and micropalaeontology library
records.type: historical slide collection + downloadable catalogue + specialist library
records.holdings: The NHM foraminifera collection includes the Heron-Allen subcollection of 740 slides. It contains material from historic expeditions including HMS Challenger and Terra Nova, and the Museum publishes a complete catalogue as an Excel spreadsheet. The associated Heron-Allen Library preserves literature tied to the foraminifera collections.
records.research_use: A digitally tractable route from nineteenth-century expedition material to slide registration, collector/donor information, locality, later specialist custody, and documentary literature. It is especially useful for studying how field/expedition specimens were transformed into long-lived slide collections.
records.access: Collection database and spreadsheet catalogue online; research access through NHM micropalaeontology curators.

records.institution: National Museum of American History — Archives Center
records.type: retrospective microscopy research archive + trade literature
records.holdings: The Richards collection comprises 6 cubic feet in 18 boxes and includes historical microscopy files, scholarly and trade publications, photographs, correspondence, advertising clippings, bibliographies, photographic slides, and a card catalogue. Its Topics in Microscopy series contains material dated from 1887 onward.
records.research_use: A reverse-bibliography and trade-history archive rather than a nineteenth-century slide provenance archive in itself. It can identify commercial literature, company histories, historical images, and references that can be chased back to contemporary makers and surviving objects.
records.access: Finding aid online; in-person research through the NMAH Archives Center by appointment.
